Modeling Approach: Exact decomposition, weights with the precision of the data. Solution chain: weights from the frequency rule, placed by fixing by unique subset sums (sparse); Birkhoff algorithm with the zeroing rule, beam search over zeroing steps, SAT re-optimization of the tail, large neighborhood search (dense). Bound chain in the same run: degree, two-line bound, SAT certificates
Workflow: Parallel run (6 threads): solution chain and bound chain in one run, stopping when they meet; final solution found by: enumeration of weight sets and largest weight first
Hardware Specifications: Apple MacBook Pro, M4 Pro (8 performance + 4 efficiency cores), 24 GB RAM
Remarks: Exact decomposition (no tolerance), with weights of the precision of the data (integers at the given scale). Proofs of optimality by the degree or two-line bound hold for real weights too; proofs by SAT certificates (small dense instances) hold for weights of this precision. 5 independent runs with the seeds 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. A run: 60 s per instance; without a proof of optimality, a second round of 600 s; the result of the run is the shorter decomposition of the two rounds, with the runtime and time to solution of its round. Best Objective Value: the shortest decomposition over the runs. Optimality Bound: the largest lower bound over the runs. Total Runtime and Time to Solution: means over the 5 runs; the time to solution of a run is the time at which it found its own final decomposition. CPU Runtime: the measured CPU time of all threads, mean over the runs with the seeds 1 to 4 (the CPU time of the run with seed 0 was not measured). The objective time series has one entry per run.
